transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-20 08:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Laura Kim (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO - ArborAI), Rina Sethi (Platform), Carlos Mendez (ML Eng), Jen Wu (Security)
Recording: recorded locally (fireflies)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 3-4 week POC focused on steady reserved GPUs for daytime traffic plus a burst pool for traffic spikes. Success criteria: p95 latency under degradation threshold, cost delta vs current infra < 30%, no data leakage, smooth failover to quantized fallback model under heavy load.

Topics covered:
- Current production traffic shape and peak patterns
- Reserved vs burst pool sizing and billing model
- Fallback policies (quantized model, CPU soft-fallback, queuing)
- Benchmark plan and telemetry to capture (latency percentiles, tokens/s, GPU util, KV hit rate)
- Security/SSO/KMS needs
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making time, i'm laura with redwood inference. quick roll call?
[00:12] Marcus (ArborAI): hey laura, marcus here. rina and carlos on my side, jen from security joining in a bit.
[00:20] Rina: hi, morning.
[00:22] Laura: great. devon and maya with me from se side. goal for today is to agree on success criteria and the capacity plan for the proof-of-concept.
[00:33] Devon (Redwood SE): just to frame it — we typically do reserved capacity for baseline throughput and a burst pool for spikes, plus a fallback chain. we want to size both parts against your observed workload.
[00:45] Carlos: yes, our baseline is about 55 rps during business hours, avg payload ~450 tokens, with a big asynchronous batch at 02:00 daily that can push lots of requests. spikes happen unpredictably roughly once a week up to ~250 rps for 3-10 minutes.
[01:05] Devon: perfect, that's super helpful. so ballpark, for baseline you want N GPUs to keep p95 under your target — what's your p95 target?
[01:15] Marcus: our product team asked for p95 under 700 ms for interactive prompts up to 512 tokens. for longer generative jobs we accept higher latency but want predictable SLAs.
[01:28] Maya (Redwood SE): ok p95 700 ms is reasonable to scope. one immediate question — are you tied to a single accelerator type? h100 vs a100 changes throughput and quantization tradeoffs.
[01:40] Rina: we currently have a mix; most infra runs on A100 80GB, but we can take h100 for new stuff if it's within cost. security prefers fewer vendors but performance will matter.
[01:52] Devon: good to know. for the POC we recommend reserving 2x A100-class nodes for steady state and enabling a burst pool of 4 additional GPUs (H100 or A100 flex) to cover 4-5x spikes. fallback plan is to route to a quantized 4-bit variant (same family) or to CPU-based batched workers for non-interactive jobs.
[02:18] Carlos: curious about the quantized model quality loss — we rely on output fidelity for ranking and cannot have >5% regression on our eval set.
[02:28] Devon: yep that's why we run a quality regression test as part of the benchmark. we include a validation set and compute rouge/bleu/embedding-sim similarity on sampled completions. if regression exceeds threshold we won't do automatic fallback — we'll keep in reserved pool or use canary routing.
[02:45] Marcus: about cost, can you give an example of how reserved + burst billing shows up? we want to compare to our current on-demand cluster costs.
[02:55] Laura: we'll share the reserved pricing matrix but in the POC we'll run an experiment: emulate your baseline for 48 hours and run two artificial spikes to show delta. we'll provide an itemized token & GPU-hour breakdown.
[03:12] Jen (Security): quick security note — we need KMS integration for customer keys, SAML SSO for admin console, and audit logs for all inference calls. also data residency question — logs must stay in us-west region.
[03:27] Maya: we support KMS and can keep logs regionally. i'll attach our security datasheet and redacted SOC2.
[03:35] Rina: great. about autoscaling — we do not want scale up latency causing user-visible errors; how do you handle warm-up and queueing?
[03:45] Devon: two mechanisms — pre-warm policy and request queueing. pre-warm spins burst GPUs based on predictive rules (time-of-day + traffic signals). queueing enforces a short backpressure window (e.g., 2-4s) and then triggers fallback if requests exceed queue thresholds. we can also use graceful degradation: switch to shorter-response mode or cached completions for known prompts.
[04:05] Carlos: can you quantify warm-up times? if we spin an extra A100, how long to be ready?
[04:12] Devon: cold start for a full model load is typically 20-60s depending on model size; with continuous batching and preloaded KV cache it's often under 30s. that's why burst pool stays on a standby fraction to reduce cold starts.
[04:28] Marcus: okay — we want a rule of thumb: keep 30% headroom in reserved to handle small spikes, use burst pool for 3-10 minute large events, and have quantized fallback for sustained overload. sound right?
[04:40] Laura: yes that's a good canonical policy. for the POC we'll test three scenarios: baseline steady load, short spikes (3-10 min), and prolonged high load to validate fallback quality and cost.
[04:55] Devon: benchmark plan details — phase 1: baseline run at 60 rps for 2 hours to measure p50/p95/p99 and token consumption; phase 2: 5x spike for 10 minutes to validate autoscale and warm-up; phase 3: quality regression run on 500 sample prompts against quantized models. we'll collect GPU util, KV hit rate, latency distribution, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:22] Carlos: what tooling will you use to run this? we want to use our telemetry (datadog) and also have you push metrics to a test prometheus endpoint.
[05:32] Devon: we can stream metrics to your prometheus or mirror into datadog; we'll provide our harness as a docker image and also a small k6 script. it's the same harness we've used for other enterprise POCs.
[05:45] Rina: about fallback — if quantized output fails quality checks, do you queue to reserved or degrade feature? we need deterministic behavior for user-facing flows.
[05:56] Maya: we can configure route priorities: 1) reserved full-precision, 2) burst full-precision, 3) quantized same-model (if quality within threshold), 4) CPU batched (non-interactive), 5) reject/soft-failure with clear error message. these are parameterizable per route.
[06:16] Marcus: timeline wise, what do you need from us to kick off next week?
[06:21] Laura: to run benchmarks next Tue (12/28) we need sample payloads, traffic distribution, and a test account with SSO or API key. also confirmation on which GPU type you prefer for burst (H100 or A100).
[06:35] Carlos: we'll send payloads and token histogram by Wed 12/22. H100 would be preferred if cost is similar.
[06:43] Jen: on security, we'll start with the questionnaire and scooped SOC2 docs; can you provide the encryption-at-rest specifics?
[06:51] Maya: yes i'll attach encryption specifics in the security packet — KMS integration modes (customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed) and TLS in transit notes.
[07:02] Laura: okay i'm going to run through some risk scenarios quickly — what happens if burst capacity is exhausted across the region?
[07:09] Devon: we have multi-variant fallback: cross-region routing if acceptable for latency, fallback to quantized models, or execute backlog queuing with SLA-based drop thresholds. we can also set up pre-purchased burst credits to prioritize your traffic.
[07:28] Marcus: cross-region is risky due to data residency. we would prefer fallback and queuing inside us-west.
[07:35] Laura: noted. we'll avoid cross-region for the POC unless you explicitly allow it.
[07:41] Rina: is there any way to simulate on-prem conditions or private VPC for the POC? we want to ensure networking and egress policies are ok before a Private deployment.
[07:51] Devon: yes we can run the POC using a VPC peering setup or private endpoints. it's slightly more setup but doable; we can run initial benchmark over an internet route then repeat with VPC-peered endpoints for a final verification.
[08:05] Carlos: good. one more — how do you measure cache effectiveness? we have lots of repeated prefixes due to prompt templates.
[08:12] Maya: we'll instrument KV cache hit ratio and show token-savings; typical prefix caching can cut token spend by 15-40% depending on duplication. we'll include that in the cost breakdown.
[08:24] Marcus: okay i'm comfortable with that plan. any other blockers?
[08:29] Jen: only the SOC2 and KMS confirmation — once we get the security packet we'll review.
[08:35] Laura: perfect. let's recap next steps...
[08:40] Devon: recap: redwood to run benchmark on 12/28, customer to supply payloads by 12/22, redwood to share pricing and SOW draft by 12/23, security docs by redwood and questionnaire completion by arborai.
[08:54] Marcus: sounds good. thanks all.
[09:00] Laura: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the harness link.
[54:30] [call end]
